reviews.consumers: First-four-foundational-area gap audit; proposed coverage only, with no new entry adoption.
reviews.outcome: Equational consequence and its own deduction rules are distinct from finite ground congruence closure and syntactic unification. The quotient-term construction supports a logical-consequence entry using the existing term, substitution, equality and quotient foundations. The corpus should prove the needed substitution-stable congruence construction locally; HSP, variety theory and the later minimal-subvariety results are outside this selection. No defect found in the selected completeness argument.

reviews.checked_passages: Adoption reuses the scoped 2012-update chapterII section14 assessment, printed pp93–96, Theorems14.12,14.17,14.19 and Definitions14.13–14.18. The selected derivation/congruence/quotient arguments were directly reconfirmed; no HSP or variety-classification extension.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found. The corpus uses an explicit finite six-rule proof calculus on a nonempty variable term algebra, proves arbitrary-valuation satisfaction by representative substitution, gives the specified canonical countermodel and extracts finite premise sets. Countable variables do not restrict signature size. Ordinary algebraic examples and the larger universal-algebra development remain excluded.
